Q: Cognee 0.5.1 - TypeError: MilvusAdapter.init() got an unexpected keyword argument 'database_name' A:

The problem is a signature mismatch between cognee core and the community Milvus adapter.

You should upgrade the adapter package.

pip install -U cognee-community-vector-adapter-milvus

Q: Bulk-load large graphs into FalkorDB A:

The bulk-loader is the most efficient way to load such bulk see: https://docs.falkordb.com/integration/bulk-loader.html

Or you can use the CSV LOAD command which can give you more flexibility see: https://docs.falkordb.com/cypher/load-csv.html

Q: Capture program stdout and stderr to separate variables A:

Since PowerShell 7.6 one can use PSRedirectToVariable feature, for example:

dir ~, invalid_path 1>variable:stdout 2>variable:stderr
$stdout
$stderr

Q: i need help in connceting to s3 bucket using snowflake? A:

Almost certainly a mismatch between your trust policy and the actual current integration values. Every time you CREATE OR REPLACE a storage integration, Snowflake generates a new IAM user ARN and external ID even if the SQL looks the same. Your trust policy is probably still pointing at old values.

Run this

DESC STORAGE INTEGRATION ZOMATO_S3_INT;

Pick STORAGE_AWS_IAM_USER_ARN and STORAGE_AWS_EXTERNAL_ID from above output, and make sure your role's trust policy uses those exact values, not whatever you had before.

Q: Difference between claude.ai vs platform.claude.com A:

You ask a question (two or three strictly, but I can see how those three lines boild down to one question). Then you do a lot of what looks like answering. I.e. most of the body of your question does not support the asking. This is a pattern often encountered in post which spam or prepare spam. It increases the risk of people getting distracted from actually participating in the discussion. You might hence want to edit and focus your question on asking - and maybe asking a more focused question. The answering part might be better received in the discussion part below.

Q: Logic used behind Array Manipulation of HackerRank A:

instead of adding k to all the elements within a range from a to b in an array, accumulate the difference array

Whenever we add anything at any index into an array and apply prefix sum algorithm the same element will be added to every element till the end of the array.

ex- n=5, m=1, a=2 b=5 k=5

    i     0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6   //take array of size N+2 to avoid index out of bound
  A[i]    0     0     0     0     0     0     0

Add k=5 to at a=2

A[a]=A[a]+k // start index from where k element should be added similar to a[p]+=sum;

     i    0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6 
   A[i]   0     0     5     0     0     0     0

now apply prefix sum algorithm

     i    0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6 
  A[i]    0     0     5     5     5     5     5

so you can see K=5 add to all the element till the end after applying prefix sum but we don't have to add k till the end. so to negate this effect we have to add -K also after b+1 index so that only from [a,b] range only will have K element addition effect.

A[b+1]=A[b]-k // to remove the effect of previously added k element after bth index.(same as a[q+1]-=sum;) that's why adding -k in the initial array along with +k.

    i    0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6 
  A[i]   0     0     5     0     0     0    -5

Now apply prefix sum Array

    i    0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6 
  A[i]   0     0     5     5     5     5     0

You can see now K=5 got added from a=2 to b=5 which was expected. Here we are only updating two indices for every query so complexity will be O(1).

Now apply the same algorithm in the input

         # 0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6    //taken array of size N+2 to avoid index out of bound
5 3      # 0     0     0     0     0     0     0
1 2 100  # 0    100    0   -100    0     0     0       
2 5 100  # 0    100   100  -100    0     0   -100
3 4 100  # 0    100   100    0     0  -100   -100

To calculate the max prefix sum, accumulate the difference array to 𝑁 while taking the maximum accumulated prefix.

After performing all the operation now apply prefix sum Array

    i      0.....1.....2.....3.....4.....5.....6 
  A[i]     0     100   200  200   200   100    0

Now you can traverse this array to find max which is 200. traversing the array will take O(N) time and updating the two indices for each query will take O(1)* number of queries(m)

overall complexity=O(N)+O(M) = O(N+M)

it means = (10^7+10^5) which is less than 10^8 (per second)
